title: Throughput Efficiency Sprint: Initiative to Reduce Token Cost via Hyper-Batching, Predictive KV Caching, and Adaptive Quantization
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Initiative to produce a repeatable playbook and rollout plan that reduces per-token serving cost for typical chat and summarization workloads. Focus areas are: 1) hyper-batching (dynamic micro-batch sizing + latency SLO preservation), 2) predictive KV cache priming and eviction heuristics, and 3) adaptive quantization profiles per model-family and sequence length. Deliverables: playbook doc, telemetry dashboards, safe rollout A/B plan, and two pilot rollouts in Hosted and Dedicated environments.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published and reviewed by Eng/Research/Console teams
Dashboard showing baseline vs optimized P95 latency and cost-per-1k-tokens for pilot workloads
Pilot rollout reduces cost-per-token by >= 20% for chat benchmarks while keeping 95th latency regression <= 10%
Automated canary gates implemented to rollback if quality regressions exceed thresholds
Operational runbook for Dedicated customers describing defaults and tunables

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Hyper-batching increases tail latency for small conversational requests. Mitigation: latency-aware scheduler that favors low-latency buckets and enforces per-route SLOs.

Risk: Quantization profiles may produce subtle quality regressions on edge prompts. Mitigation: conservative profile selection, automated human-in-the-loop evals, and automatic fallback to FP16 model if quality drops detected.
Risk: KV caching priming could leak state between tenants in Dedicated if misconfigured. Mitigation: enforce strict tenant isolation in KV namespace and add audit checks in deploy pipeline.
Risk: Operational complexity for customers. Mitigation: publish a clear defaults-first playbook and Console UI toggles that surface safe presets.
